author: Tara Viswanathan
text:
Weekly planning structure I created 8+ yrs ago and still use 

- 4 main buckets 
- 3-5 goals in each bucket
- top 3 things I need to accomplish this week 
- read every morning and evening 
- check off progress through the week

Sunday evening routine, here we go!

topReplies.author: Tara Viswanathan
topReplies.text:
Pt 2: to be filled in during the week  admin work, unexpected stuff that came up, and a laundry list of things that happened so I can jog my memory when the week ends (or thereafter in quarterly reflections) 

And that’s it — super simple but super effective

topReplies.author: Adrián
topReplies.text: Not bad, but I prefer my strategy …

topReplies.author: Nihal Pai
topReplies.text: OOC What’s the difference between “things that happened” and “stuff that came up”?

topReplies.author: Tara Viswanathan
topReplies.text:
things that happened = recount of the stuff that happened that week "met w x person" etc. just having a record helps me when i go back and recap the week on Sunday night. 

stuff that came up = stuff i didn't expect that threw me off my plans / schedule

topReplies.author: Zach
topReplies.text: This is amazing, people try to complicate their plan so much because it makes them feel like they are doing something (the plan) but in reality the most simple plan is usually the best because you immediately can execute on it. We use a very similar idea in the military OPorder

topReplies.author: Tara Viswanathan
topReplies.text:
100% agree! that's why i've kept it up so long. 

keeping it simple is hard though, and I think a lot of ppl miss that. It actually takes a good amount of brain power to figure out what to put in here. (takes me 45 min to 1 hr to form this -- including reflection from last week)
